h: Seeing That Every Blessing Leads to Hearing Torah

p: רְאֵה אָנֹכִי נוֹתֵן וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים יא, כו)
that you will hearken to the commandments," etc.
"and the curse, if you do not hearken,"
whereas for the blessing it says,
that although there are mentioned in the blessings
nevertheless the essence of the blessing is
"that you will hearken to the commandments of Hashem";
as we find in Parashas Eikev,
"And He will bless the fruit of your womb
and the fruit of your land," etc.,
"There will not be among you a barren man or woman";
and it is expounded in the Gemara (Bechoros 44b):
"'There will not be among you a barren man':
that your prayer will not be barren
to the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer,
which is the whole strength of Yisrael,
who are likened to a worm,
whose strength is only in its mouth,
and it strikes the cedars with its mouth,
And it is written after it (ibid. 7:15):
"And Hashem will remove from you all sickness";
and it is expounded (Yerushalmi Shabbos, chapter 14,
as referring to the yetzer hara,
whose beginning is sweet and whose end is bitter.
And it uses the expression "all sickness,"
along the lines of what it says
"And you shall serve Hashem your God,
and He will bless your bread and your water,
and I will remove sickness from your midst";
and it is found in the Gemara (Bava Kamma 92b):
"eighty-three kinds of illness are in it:
machalah is that number in gematria."
And this follows what it says
the gall casts a drop into it
the root of anger is from the gall.
And anger is the root of the yetzer hara,
all kinds of Gehinnom rule over him";
he can come to all kinds of sins,
all kinds of Gehinnom rule over him.
And this is what it says,
And this is what it says, "all sickness":
that is, all kinds of Gehinnom.
And it says, "and He will bless your bread":
when the blessing is from Hashem Yisbarach,
"I will remove sickness from your midst."
וְכֵן וְהֵסִיר ה׳ מִמְּךָ כָּל חוֹלִי
So too "And Hashem will remove from you all sickness":
for what comes from Hashem Yisbarach
אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא דָּבָר רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
does not bring anything bad, chas v'shalom.
"And you shall serve Hashem your God,"
"and He will bless your bread," etc.,
"And Hashem your God will keep for you," etc.,
that at first, before the blessing,
they are still in the aspect of "many,"
not on the level of "as one man";
as one man with one heart,
as we find at Matan Torah,
and they expounded in the Mechilta:
for they are not yet as one man;
"and He will bless your bread and your water,"
Hashem Yisbarach allots his allotted bread
for words of Torah and service.
"and I will remove sickness from your midst":
as one man with one heart;
and therefore the singular is written.
for at first they are still
as one man with one heart;
and therefore all the blessings are written
which speaks of the blessings and the opposite
that will be given to them afterward
on Mount Gerizim and Mount Eival,
which they have not yet received:
it is written in the plural,
that at first they are still
not on the level of "as one man,"
as long as they have not heard
this refers to an individual soul;
for there is one who sees beforehand,
that they help bring into their heart
and to empty out the evil,
"and He will remove from you all sickness,"
וְאַף אִם יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה נְפָשׁוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ
And even if there are many such souls
they are all included as one,
as one man with one heart,
with the perfect souls of Yisrael.
and to them it says in the singular, "See":
that they see this at once,
which is what will be afterward,
when they will be given to them
for then they will all be as one man.
וְכֵן פָּתַח בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ
And so the Midrash Rabbah on this parashah opens:
"I set before you" for the future.
that it is for the good,
which is the good way that they should choose."
And on Shabbos every person merits
to see that everything is for the good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פט, א)
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest," etc.,
as referring to the day of Shabbos,
which is the "day that He gives rest";
in the midst of the hard labor
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach
and is only for the good,
and he has rest "from your trembling,"
which is from the agitation of the yetzer hara

Removing the Illness of the Yetzer Hara
Seeing the Good Before It Arrives
